Identify product containing named element for each reaction and determine its magnetic properties (diamagnetic vs paramagnetic). Diamagnetic if all electrons paired; paramagnetic if any unpaired electrons.
(i) NH3 burning with O2 gives N2 (or NO). Typical combustion of NH3 gives N2 and H2O; N2 is diamagnetic (all electrons paired).
(ii) Cr2O7^2- reduced by H+ gives Cr^3+ (d^3). Cr3+ has three unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.
(iii) Cu2+ with excess KCN forms [Cu(CN)4]2- (Cu+ complex). Cu+ is d^10 → all electrons paired → diamagnetic.
(iv) HCO2^- with conc H2SO4 warm gives CO2 (or possibly formate oxidation). CO2 is diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons).
(v) Cr3+ with H2O2 in NaOH oxidizes Cr3+ to CrO4^2- (Cr6+ d0) or Cr2O7^2-; Cr(VI) has no unpaired electrons → diamagnetic? However typical alkaline medium reduces? Reaction: Cr3+ + H2O2 + OH- → CrO4^2- (Cr(VI)). Cr(VI) oxoanions are generally diamagnetic (d0). But need check: CrO4^2- (Cr6+) is d0 → diamagnetic. However some might think paramagnetic? d0 has no unpaired electrons → diamagnetic.
(vi) FeS2 roasting gives Fe2O3 (or FeO) and SO2. Fe3+ (d5) has five unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.
Now count diamagnetic products: (i) N2 diamag, (iii) Cu+ diamag, (iv) CO2 diamag, (v) CrO4^2- diamag. That's 4. But need ensure correctness: (i) combustion of NH3 may produce NO rather than N2 if incomplete; but typical 'burning' of NH3 with O2 gives N2 and H2O (complete). So N2 diamag.
(ii) paramag.
(iii) diamag.
(iv) diamag.
(v) diamag.
(vi) paramag.
Thus 4 diamagnetic reactions.
However some may argue CrO4^2- is paramagnetic? No, d0 is diamagnetic. So answer 4.
But check (v): Cr3+ + H2O2 + NaOH → CrO4^2-? Reaction: Cr3+ + H2O2 + OH- → CrO4^2- + H2O. Yes oxidation to Cr(VI). Cr(VI) oxoanions are diamagnetic.
Thus 4 diamagnetic.
Answer integer 4.
